results.term_definition: A star with spectral type "F". Astronomers identify F-type stars by the presence of moderately strong ionized calcium lines and some other atomic metal lines and the weak hydrogen absorption lines in their spectra. They have typical (effective) temperatures between around 6000 kelvins (K) and 7400 K. Compared to other stars, they appear white or yellowish white to human eyes unless interstellar or atmospheric reddening is important. Polaris (the North Star) is an example of an F-type star.
